Wall Street economists had forecast a March trade deficit of $10.3 billion.
The volume of total crude and petroleum product imports rose in March to 302.8 million barrels from 264.8 million in February. The total value rose to $5.81 billion in March from $5.57 billion.
The price of imported crude oil fell to an average $18.72 a barrel in March from $20.49 a barrel in February. The value of March crude oil imports rose to $4.38 billion from $4.22 billion.

The department said that U.S. exports of nonmonetary gold rose by $720 million in March to $1.09 billion. The gold, which had been held by foreign governments and other agencies in the vault of the New York Federal Reserve Bank, was shipped to the United Kingdom and Switzerland, a department official said.
U.S. imports of cars and car parts tumbled by $1.2 billion. The main drop of such imports occurred from Canada.

The balance-of-payments basis for recording U.S. trade via receipts from and payments to other countries includes adjustments for military shipments, nonmonetary gold, and inland freight trade with Canada and Mexico.
Census basis data uses information collected by the U.S. Customs Service on goods shipped across U.S. borders.
